answer: Each identity registers one harbor beacon, locks an 80-credit bond, and files serial, power, and distance to the harbor station. The harbor auditor recomputes the signal level at the horizon from a signal-propagation table keyed by power and distance. A mismatch over 4 percent, a reused serial, or no filing burns the bond. The first filing costs 35 credits; the kth costs 35+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7028 and 1000 fakes pay 3,531,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-beacon ring fails because one serial binds one identity and a repeat filing burns both bonds. Honest identities pay 35 once.
